entries.clue: Bran flakes maybe are lying about (5)

blocks.note: to fib is to tell a small lie

annotation.surface: Someone claims a breakfast cereal's promises are untrue.
annotation.walkthrough: The definition is by example, flagged by 'maybe': bran flakes are one source of fibre.
annotation.definitionFit: Bran flakes are a classic high-fibre food, so they exemplify fibre.

entries.clue: Engineer cut down below sign (5,7)

indicatorNotes.below: in a down clue, the first piece sits under the second

blocks.note: to frank a letter is to stamp or sign it
to whittle is to pare down with a knife

annotation.surface: An engineer is demoted or cut to size beneath a signpost.
annotation.walkthrough: Sir Frank Whittle invented the jet engine. 'Below' puts WHITTLE underneath FRANK in the grid.
annotation.definitionFit: Frank Whittle was the British engineer who invented the turbojet engine.

entries.clue: Recycled reticule with weapon kept in drawer (3,6)

indicatorNotes.Recycled: the letters go round: the back half of NETBAG moves to the front
indicatorNotes.kept in: ARM is held inside the cycled word

blocks.note: a reticule is a small net bag

annotation.surface: A weapon is hidden in a drawer inside an old handbag.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Drawer' is not furniture: a magnet draws iron towards it.
annotation.definitionFit: A bar magnet attracts, or draws, metal, so it is a drawer.

entries.clue: In retirement old books are a source of inspiration (5)

indicatorNotes.In retirement: retiring means going back, so the letters run backwards

annotation.surface: A retired person finds old books inspiring.
annotation.walkthrough: Erato is the Greek Muse of lyric and love poetry; Muses are the classic sources of inspiration.
annotation.definitionFit: Erato is one of the nine Muses, who inspired poets and artists.

entries.clue: New thick cover seen all over nestling bird (8)

indicatorNotes.nestling: U settles inside, between N and THATCH

blocks.note: a thick covering of straw, or of hair
U is the film certificate for 'universal': fit to be seen by all

annotation.surface: A bird nests under a fresh thatched roof that is visible everywhere.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Nestling bird' reads as a chick; 'nestling' is really the instruction for U to sit inside.
annotation.definitionFit: The nuthatch is a small tree-climbing bird.

entries.clue: Trump’s tuppenny-ha’penny copshop lined dame up (6-3-4)

indicatorNotes.shop: to shop someone is to turn them in, and a shaken-up order of letters follows
indicatorNotes.up: 'shop … up' reads like 'shake up': the letters of 'lined dame' are stirred into a new order

blocks.note: to cop and to nick both mean to take or steal

annotation.surface: A petty-minded American leader's police station puts a lady in a line-up.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Copshop' looks like one word for a police station, but it splits: 'cop' is a verb and 'shop' pairs with 'up'. Tuppenny-ha'penny is British for cheap and trivial; 'Trump's' asks for the US version.
annotation.definitionFit: The American idiom for something petty and cheap, as tuppenny-ha'penny is the British one; Trump stands for the US.

entries.clue: McFly perhaps turning it up satisfied one repeatedly doing twist? (4,9)

indicatorNotes.turning: turning means going back, so IT runs backwards
indicatorNotes.up: in a down clue, reading upwards reverses

blocks.note: to meet a need is to satisfy it
to ravel is to twist and tangle; one doing it is a raveller

annotation.surface: A pop singer keeps performing the Twist and is happy about it.
annotation.walkthrough: Marty McFly travels through time in the film Back to the Future. 'Twist' suggests the dance, but it is the tangling kind.
annotation.definitionFit: Marty McFly is the hero of Back to the Future, who travels in time; 'perhaps' marks him as an example.

entries.clue: A fine term at Harrow – but what points out consequences (9)

indicatorNotes.but: 'but' means except: Harrow without ARROW leaves H

blocks.note: an arrow points things out; HARROW minus ARROW

annotation.surface: A penalty during a school term at Harrow, a famous English public school.
annotation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'but what points out' look like a new thought, yet it tells you to take ARROW out of HARROW.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: what follows an event, originally the second crop of grass after mowing.

entries.clue: Recognise member of European nobility (5)

blocks.note: to regard or accept as valid
a Continental nobleman, equal to an earl

annotation.surface: Someone learns to identify aristocrats.
annotation.walkthrough: The surface runs the two halves together as 'identify a noble', but they are separate senses: to count someone as a friend is to recognise them as one.
annotation.definitionFit: To count something as valid is to recognise it; a count is a European noble.

entries.clue: Fairy-tale outcome, naked man with heavenly body bordering on regret (1,5,4,4)

indicatorNotes.bordering: ADAM goes round the edges of RE

blocks.note: the first man, naked in Eden
a comet is a body in the heavens

annotation.surface: A naked man gazes at a star and wishes for a happy ending.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Bordering on regret' reads as a phrase, but 'on' is the piece that ADAM borders, and 'regret' is a separate piece.
annotation.definitionFit: Fairy tales end with wishes granted, a dream come true.

entries.clue: Extreme disquiet did prevail, according to hearsay (12)

indicatorNotes.according to hearsay: RAINED is said the same as REIGNED

annotation.surface: Rumour says that severe unrest was widespread.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Extreme disquiet' reads as one phrase; 'Extreme' is the definition on its own.
annotation.definitionFit: Unrestrained behaviour goes to extremes, held back by nothing.

entries.clue: Warned by horn, flabby person’s knocked down crossing (8)

indicatorNotes.crossing: KD reaches across LAX ONE, enclosing it

blocks.note: the auctioneer's abbreviation for knocked down, sold
one = a person; the 's is 'is', a link

annotation.surface: A fat pedestrian gets run over at a crossing after a car's horn sounds.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Knocked down crossing' paints a road accident; KD is the auction abbreviation for a lot knocked down.
annotation.definitionFit: A klaxon is a loud warning horn, so to be klaxoned is to be warned by one.

entries.clue: It’s charged for fashionable types (6)

blocks.note: the ton was high society, the fashionable set

annotation.surface: Something is priced specially for trendy people.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Charged' suggests a price; here it is electric charge.
annotation.definitionFit: A proton carries a positive electric charge.

entries.clue: Manually construct labels seen in bathroom water structure (9)

blocks.note: H and C: the hot and cold labels on taps
a raft is built to float on water

annotation.surface: Someone builds a raft by hand, using tap labels from the bathroom.
annotation.walkthrough: British taps are often marked H and C, read here as 'H and C'.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: 'hand' matches 'manually' and 'craft' matches 'construct'.

entries.clue: MP that whip’s feeding on cheese (9)

indicatorNotes.feeding on: CAT takes MEMBER inside it, as if eating

annotation.surface: A party whip is keeping an MP in line.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Whip' in a parliamentary setting suggests a party enforcer; here it is the cat, the flogging whip.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: a soft Normandy cheese is one kind of cheese.

entries.clue: See 5
The writer is going to read out passage (5)

indicatorNotes.read out: reading something out means saying it, so we want a word that sounds like the phrase

blocks.note: the writer = I, is going to = WILL: I'LL

annotation.surface: An author is about to give a reading from a passage.
annotation.walkthrough: I'LL, spoken, is AISLE. 'Passage' looks like a passage of text, but it is a walkway.
annotation.definitionFit: An aisle is a passage between rows of seats.

entries.clue: Know-all Special Constable arresting market porter? (5,4)

indicatorNotes.arresting: SC holds MART ALE in custody, inside it

annotation.surface: A volunteer policeman who thinks he knows everything arrests a market porter.
annotation.walkthrough: A market porter carries goods, but here 'porter' is the beer; the question mark flags the split. A Special Constable is a volunteer British police officer.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: both name a person who shows off superior knowledge.

entries.clue: Venerated species? Quickly count how many (5)

blocks.note: to tot up is to add up a quick sum

annotation.surface: Someone is asked for a quick headcount of a sacred animal.
annotation.walkthrough: TOT 'EM means 'add them up'. The question mark flags that a totem is often an animal species revered by a clan.
annotation.definitionFit: A totem is an animal or plant revered as a clan's emblem.

entries.clue: My beloved Music Faculty, and what it does through data transmission (4,5)

indicatorNotes.through: EAR and HEAR pass inside the outer letters
indicatorNotes.data transmission: the first letters of these two words, D and T

blocks.note: an ear for music is a faculty
what an ear does is hear

annotation.surface: A university music department sends a message by modem to someone dear.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Music Faculty' looks like a university department; it is the ear, the faculty used for music.
annotation.definitionFit: Dear heart is an old endearment meaning my beloved.

entries.clue: Contrarily starts to eat meat – and umpteen set veg (6)

indicatorNotes.Contrarily: everything is put the other way round
indicatorNotes.starts to: take the first letters of the next words

blocks.note: first letters of eat, meat, umpteen

annotation.surface: An awkward diner eats meat while a mound of vegetables sits untouched.
annotation.walkthrough: The 'and' sits among the starting words but only eat, meat and umpteen supply letters.
annotation.definitionFit: A legume, such as a pea or bean, is a vegetable.

entries.clue: Fool rolling barrel over lady’s fingers (5)

blocks.note: a mug is a fool; reversed

annotation.surface: A clumsy person trips on a rolling barrel that runs over a woman's hand.
annotation.walkthrough: Lady's fingers is the British name for okra; gumbo is another name for it.
annotation.definitionFit: Gumbo is another name for okra, known in Britain as lady's fingers.

entries.clue: Surgeon you shouldn’t have taken around to put a stop to feud (8)

indicatorNotes.taken around: to take someone around is to lead them in a circle, so VET goes round END

blocks.note: ta is British for thanks, said when given a present

annotation.surface: An unwelcome surgeon is brought in to settle a long quarrel.
annotation.walkthrough: 'You shouldn't have' is what you say on receiving a gift, a way of saying thanks: TA.
annotation.definitionFit: A plain synonym: a long-running blood feud, originally between Corsican or Sicilian families.

entries.clue: Worried chap might be put in the picture (5)

annotation.definition2: chap might be put in the picture

blocks.clueFragment: chap might be put in the picture
blocks.note: sketched into a picture with pencil

annotation.surface: An anxious man could do with being briefed.
annotation.walkthrough: 'Put in the picture' usually means informed; here it is literal: a chap might be drawn, sketched into a drawing.
annotation.definitionFit: Drawn describes a worried, strained look, and also something sketched.
annotation.definitionNote: The second definition is a clause: a chap might be drawn.

entries.clue: See 4
Measure of liquid being seaweedy, litre one’s about to drink (8,6)

indicatorNotes.to drink: I'M ON swallows the other pieces

blocks.note: a peri is a fairy being in Persian myth

annotation.surface: Someone is about to drink a litre of green, weedy liquid.
annotation.walkthrough: 'One's about to drink' reads as a plain statement of intent; really 'one's' and 'about' are two pieces that swallow the rest.
annotation.definitionFit: A definition by class: the British unit of about 4.5 litres is one measure of liquid.

entries.clue: Order two of each? Right (8)

indicatorNotes.Order: put the letters in a new order

annotation.surface: A shopper checks they are ordering a pair: two of each.
annotation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: shoes are ordered in pairs, two of each, one left and one right.
annotation.definitionFit: Footwear comes in pairs, two of each item.

entries.clue: Battery stereo system finally reduced by 50% (5)

indicatorNotes.finally reduced by 50%: the last letter, M (1,000), is halved to D (500)

blocks.note: NICAM is the digital stereo system for British TV sound

annotation.surface: A stereo's battery life is cut in half.
annotation.walkthrough: Read the letters as Roman numerals: halving the final M gives D.
annotation.definitionFit: A NiCad is a nickel-cadmium rechargeable battery.
